title: Taskiem Workflow Definition (wd/v1)
description: Canonical, versioned workflow definition. Structural rules live here; cross-reference rules (unique step ids, needs targets, cycles, expression roots) are enforced by the engine's semantic validator and documented in docs/contracts/wd-v1.md.

outputs.description: What the workflow gives back when another workflow uses it as a template step (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, callable workflows): each an expression over its own top-level steps. A workflow with outputs and an inputs schema is callable.

expr.description: CEL expression, marked by a leading '='.

connectorRef.description: Connector id pinned to a major version, e.g. paystack@1.

jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for data. Validated separately.

values.description: Object whose values are literals or expressions, at any depth.

idempotency_seed.description: Replaces the run id in the idempotency key material (docs/contracts/idempotency.md).

origin.description: Set when a template step is expanded (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, template steps): the template a step came from, the template step it came from, and its id inside the template, under which its output is kept in its scope's results. Never written by hand.

step.description: A step; 'type' selects which step schema applies.

connection.description: Connection name in the run's environment; defaults to the only one for this connector.

capability.description: Set by capability expansion, never written by hand: the step stands for a capability, its input is the capability's, and the rail's mapping turns it into the action's input and the action's output back into the capability's.

input.description: The rail's mapping to the action's input (roots: input, steps).

output.description: The rail's mapping to the capability's output (roots: input, output, steps).

steps.description: The rail's step names (steps.<name>) for a composite, by the expanded step ids they stand for.

image.description: Registry, repository and digest: registry.example.com/team/tool@sha256:<64 hex>. Tags are refused (docs/container-steps.md).

command.description: The program and its first arguments; the image's entrypoint is not used.

input_mode.description: How the step's input (JSON) reaches the program: on stdin (default) or as the file named by $TASKIEM_INPUT.

output_mode.description: Where the program writes its output (one JSON value): stdout (default) or the file named by $TASKIEM_OUTPUT.

secrets_mode.description: Declared secrets as environment variables (default) or as files in the directory named by $TASKIEM_SECRETS.

class.description: The step's effect class; unsafe_write unless declared.

network.description: none (default): no network. egress: HTTP(S) through the platform's egress proxy, to hosts on both this list and the environment's allow-list.

cpu.description: CPU cores, as Kubernetes writes them: "500m", "1", "1.5".

idempotency_header.description: Header that carries the encoded idempotency key, e.g. Idempotency-Key.

event.description: Signal name, or connector trigger as connector@major:trigger.event, e.g. paystack@1:transfer_event.transfer.success

policy.description: Named approval policy, or a built-in: single, maker_checker.

subject.description: Data shown to approvers; recorded with each decision.

subflowStep.description: Runs another workflow of the business as its own run, a child of this one (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, subflow steps): input is the child's run inputs; with wait (the default) the step waits for the child to end and its output is {run_id, status, outputs}; without, it completes once the child has started.

workflow.description: The workflow's id (the business's own; it must have a published version and a manual or subflow trigger).

version.description: A version to run; without it, the version published when the step starts.

aiStep.description: Asks an AI model at run time and gets a typed answer (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, AI steps): the prompt and input, with personal data masked, go to the deployment's model; the output is the answer, matching output_schema.

prompt.description: What to ask the model: text, or an expression (=...) over this workflow. Personal data in it is masked.

output_schema.description: The answer's shape: an object schema; the step's output is the answer, checked against it.

model.description: A model this deployment offers for AI steps; without it, the deployment's default.

personal_data.description: Input fields whose personal data reaches the model as it is (decision 0050). Every other personal value, in the input and the prompt, is replaced by a placeholder, and put back in the answer.

methods.description: The HTTP methods the webhook takes; POST when left out. A request without a body (a GET) has its query parameters as trigger.body.

jwt.description: With auth jwt: the iss and aud the token must carry, and the algorithms allowed (by default those the key fits).

cors.description: Web pages at these origins may call the webhook from a browser; * for any.

respond.description: The caller waits (up to 30 seconds) for a respond step's answer instead of a 202 with the run id.

options.description: Settings of the connector trigger, checked against its manifest's options schema (for a remotely registered trigger: what to subscribe to at the provider).

config.description: A form on the organisation's public storefront (docs/storefronts.md); its submissions start runs.

Starts a run in prod on one of the business's invoices (docs/invoices.md): event paid, when it is paid in full, once per invoice; event payment, for every payment counted towards it, once per payment part. trigger.body is the invoice, with the payment and its receipt for the payment event.

show_if.description: CEL over the answers of earlier pages

config.description: Starts on a rail's normalised payment events (schemas/capabilities-v1.json), whichever rail the business connected: each environment's connections whose rail sends them (or the one named).

connection.description: One connection to listen on; left out, every connection whose rail sends the events.

ussdMenu.description: A USSD menu walked at the edge (docs/ussd.md). Screen sizes, reachability, patterns, conditions and placeholders are checked by engine/wd.Validate.

to.description: Who is asked: a phone or email from the run (expressions), or a role of members

verify.description: Ask for a code sent to the same phone or email first

schema.description: The questions, as an inputs schema; the answers are the step's output

capabilityStep.description: A capability (schemas/capabilities-v1.json) done by whichever rail the connection is: expanded into that rail's own action when a run starts (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, capability steps).

connection.description: Connection name in the run's environment; defaults to the only one whose rail can do it. await_settlement and await_reversal default to the connection of the payment they follow, await_payment to that of the collect_link it waits on.

templateStep.description: A callable template (templates/, decision 0047), or a callable workflow of the business (decision 0048), used as a step: expanded into its steps when the workflow is deployed, their ids prefixed with this step's id and two underscores; the step's output is its outputs (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, template steps).

template.description: The callable template's id (templates/). Exactly one of template and workflow.

params.description: The template's parameters, as the Start page takes them: values, never expressions.

input.description: The template's run inputs, as literals or expressions over this workflow.

workflow.description: A callable workflow of the business (one with outputs and a published version): its id. Exactly one of template and workflow.

callbackStep.description: Waits for another system to call the run back (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, callback steps): the step's address, run.callbacks.<id>, is sent to that system by an earlier step; a POST to it is the step's output.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the call (default 7d).

on_timeout.description: continue: the step completes with {timed_out: true} instead of failing.

respondStep.description: Answers the webhook call that started the run (docs/contracts/wd-v1.md, respond steps): only in a workflow whose webhook trigger has respond: true. The caller gets this status, headers and body; the run carries on.

headers.description: Response headers; only Content-Type, Location, Cache-Control and X- headers are sent.

body.description: The response body: an object or list is sent as JSON, a string as text; values may be expressions.
